ios.desc:
Skip podcast ads automatically, including sponsor messages read by hosts, and get back to the shows you came to hear.

OctoCasts is an iPhone podcast player built for fewer interruptions. It finds ad breaks and skips them as you listen, while keeping you in control. Search and follow your favorite podcasts, build your queue, and choose how every show sounds.

LISTEN YOUR WAY
• Stream episodes or download them for offline listening
• Read along with transcripts that follow the episode
• Jump quickly between podcast chapters
• Build and reorder your queue
• Keep track of new, in progress, and downloaded episodes
• Change playback speed, Enhance Voices, and Shrink Silence
• Save listening settings for individual podcasts
• Set a sleep timer
• Import your subscriptions from other podcast apps
• Start without creating an account or providing an email address

FREE PLAYER, OPTIONAL PRO
The podcast player is free and includes 10 automatic ad skips each calendar month. Pro removes the monthly skip limit for unlimited automatic ad skipping.

Automatic ad skipping may occasionally miss an ad or skip something that isn’t an ad. You can turn it off, undo and report an incorrect skip, or report a missed ad from the player.

Privacy Policy: https://octocasts.com/privacy
Terms of Use: https://octocasts.com/terms

show_hn.title: Show HN: Octopoddy – iOS Podcast App Using Transcripts and LLMs to Skip Ads

quotes.text:
TL;DR
I'm a fan of podcasts and I despise ads. I built an iOS app to detect and skip in audio ad content.

Motivation:
I love podcasts, especially multi hour ones that go into detail on niche topics. One thing that puts me off some podcasts is having the flow become interrupted, especially mid sentence by dynamically inserted ads. Last year this led me down a rabbit hole of experimenting with removing ads from the podcasts I listen to.

Experimentation:
At first I tried using Whisper for ad detection to generate a transcript of an episode, then feed this to ChatGPT and ask it to find the ad timestamps. This worked surprisingly well. I had a proof of concept working but I wanted something I could actually use on my phone.

Productionization:
Next I wondered if I were to productionize my prototype how would I do that? From experimenting the main issue would be volume of audio transcription required to satisfy a moderate-heavy podcast listener. I estimated ~100 hours of audio per month would be required per user. In testing I used OpenAI hosted Whisper, charged at $0.006/min. That sounds quite cheap. What would that be for 100 hours? $0.006/min -> $0.36/hour -> $36.00/100 hours. S%#t. $36/user/month is way too expensive. If you were to turn this into a business at that rate you'd probably need to be charging at least $50/month. No one's going to pay that.
